examples.en: The content of that book is so outdated.
You should throw away those stale ideas now.

examples.ko: 창고에서 케케묵은 물건이 아주 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A lot of dusty old stuff came out of the storage room.

examples.ko: 요즘 누가 그렇게 케케묵은 농담을 해요?
examples.en: Who tells such stale jokes these days?
Everyone says that rule is antiquated.
Grandpa's room has a musty, old smell.

explain: '오래되다'는 그냥 시간이 많이 지났다는 말이고, '케케묵다'는 낡고 시대에 뒤떨어져서 별로라는 느낌이 들어 있어요. '케케묵은 생각/이야기/농담'처럼 '-은' 꼴로 많이 써요. 좋은 뜻의 오래된 물건에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '오래되다' just means a lot of time has passed, but '케케묵다' carries a negative feeling of being worn out and behind the times. It is often used in the '-은' form, as in '케케묵은 생각/이야기/농담'. You would not normally use it for something old in a good way.

examples.en: I feel uneasy after telling a lie.

examples.ko: 뭔가 켕기는 게 있는지 내 눈을 못 쳐다봐요.
examples.en: He can't look me in the eye, as if he has something to hide.

examples.ko: 줄이 너무 켕기면 끊어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the rope is pulled too tight, it can snap.

examples.ko: 친구에게 빌린 돈을 못 갚아서 계속 켕겨요.
examples.en: I keep feeling guilty because I haven't paid back the money I borrowed from my friend.

examples.ko: 켕기는 데가 없으면 왜 대답을 피해요?
examples.en: If you have nothing to feel guilty about, why do you avoid answering?

examples.ko: 그 일 때문에 마음이 켕겨서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My conscience bothered me about that, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 요즘 대화에서는 줄이나 피부가 팽팽해진다는 쪽보다 '마음이 켕기다', '켕기는 데가 있다'처럼 잘못한 일 때문에 불편하다는 쪽으로 더 많이 들어요. 비슷한 말로 '찔리다'가 있어요. 보통 '마음이'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: In conversation, you will more often hear it for an uneasy feeling about something you did wrong, as in '마음이 켕기다' or '켕기는 데가 있다', than for a rope or skin being pulled tight. A similar word is '찔리다'. It is usually paired with '마음이'.

examples.en: Snow is piled up in layers outside the window.
I put red beans in layers between the rice cakes.

examples.ko: 서랍 안에 옷을 켜켜이 쌓아 두었어요.
examples.en: I stacked the clothes in layers in the drawer.
I cleaned the bookshelf, which was covered in layers of dust.

examples.ko: 이 도시에는 오랜 역사가 켜켜이 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: A long history has built up in layers in this city.
Please pack the kimchi into the container in layers.

explain: '겹겹이'와 비슷하지만 '켜켜이'는 쌓인 층이 하나하나 보이는 느낌이에요. '쌓이다', '쌓다', '앉다'처럼 쌓이는 말과 함께 자주 써요. 먼지나 세월처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 쌓였다고 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '겹겹이', but '켜켜이' gives a feeling that you can see each layer one by one. It is often used with words about piling up, such as '쌓이다', '쌓다' and '앉다'. You can also use it for things like dust or time that have built up.

examples.en: I often wear corduroy pants in winter.
The corduroy jacket is warm and comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 코르덴 천은 만지면 결이 느껴져요.
examples.en: You can feel the ridges when you touch this corduroy fabric.
I bought a bag made of corduroy.
My father went out wearing a corduroy hat.
I turn corduroy inside out when I wash it.

explain: 세로로 골이 있는 두툼한 천이라 가을·겨울 옷에 많이 보여요. '코듀로이'라고도 해요. '코르덴 바지', '코르덴 재킷'처럼 천 이름을 옷 이름 앞에 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: It is a thick fabric with vertical ridges, so you often see it in autumn and winter clothes. It is also called '코듀로이'. People put the fabric name before the clothing name, as in '코르덴 바지' and '코르덴 재킷'.

en: stuffy nose; person with a stuffy nose

examples.en: I caught a cold, so my voice sounds stuffy.
I answered the phone in a stuffed-up voice.
My nose is blocked, so I sound stuffed up.
My younger sibling acts cute in a nasal voice.
Because of my stuffy nose, my pronunciation sounds strange.
Even though I took medicine, my stuffy nose won't get better.

explain: 코가 막혀서 소리가 코에서 막힌 듯 나오는 상태나 그런 사람을 말해요. 보통 '코맹맹이 소리'로 많이 써요. 일부러 코를 울려서 귀엽게 내는 말투를 가리킬 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a state where your nose is blocked and your voice sounds pinched, or a person in that state. It is mostly used as '코맹맹이 소리'. It can also describe a cute nasal way of talking that someone does on purpose.

examples.en: I'm crocheting a hat with a crochet hook.
I want to learn how to crochet.
I went to the shop to buy a crochet hook and yarn.
My grandmother made a tablecloth with a crochet hook.
The tip of the crochet hook is sharp, so you have to be careful.

examples.ko: 이 코바늘은 굵은 실에 쓰기 좋아요.
examples.en: This crochet hook is good for thick yarn.

explain: 대바늘은 두 개로 뜨고 코바늘은 바늘 하나로 실을 걸어 떠요. '코바늘로 뜨다', '코바늘 뜨개'처럼 '뜨다'와 함께 써요. 가방, 모자, 수세미 같은 작은 물건을 만들 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: Knitting needles (대바늘) are used in a pair, while a 코바늘 is a single needle that hooks the yarn. It is used with '뜨다', as in '코바늘로 뜨다' and '코바늘 뜨개'. People often use it to make small things like bags, hats and dish scrubbers.

examples.en: I haven't seen so much as a glimpse of my friends lately.
My son doesn't show his face even on holidays.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 한 번 가더니 코빼기도 안 보여요.
examples.en: He left once and has never shown his face since.
It's so cold that my nose turned red.

examples.ko: 이불 밖으로 코빼기만 내밀고 자고 있어요.
examples.en: He is sleeping with only his nose poking out of the blanket.

examples.ko: 방학 내내 집에 코빼기도 안 비치더니 웬일이에요?
examples.en: You didn't show up at home the whole vacation, so what brings you here?

explain: '코'를 낮추어 편하게 부르는 말이라 윗사람에게나 격식 있는 자리에서는 쓰지 않아요. 대부분 '코빼기도 안 보이다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 연락도 없이 코빼기도 안 보여요.
phrases.en: That friend doesn't show up at all, without even a call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 전혀 나타나지 않는다고 불평하거나 서운해할 때 써요. 편한 사이에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to complain or show disappointment that someone never appears. It is casual.

explain_en: It is a casual, slightly rough way to say '코' (nose), so you would not use it with elders or in formal situations. It is mostly used with negative words, as in '코빼기도 안 보이다'.

examples.en: The snotty little kid has grown into a young man before I knew it.
We have been friends since we were little kids.
Little kids are running around in the alley.

examples.ko: 그 코흘리개가 이렇게 컸다니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't believe that little kid has grown this much.

examples.ko: 코흘리개 시절 사진을 보니 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: Looking at photos from my childhood makes me laugh.
Our teacher still sees us as little kids.

explain: 아주 어린 아이를 정겹게, 때로는 얕잡아 부르는 말이에요. 어릴 때를 떠올리며 '코흘리개 시절/때'라고 많이 말해요. 어른이 어린 사람에게 쓰면 귀엽게도 무시하는 말로도 들릴 수 있어서 상황을 봐야 해요.
explain_en: It is a word for a very young child, either affectionate or a bit belittling. People often use it when recalling childhood, as in '코흘리개 시절/때'. When an adult says it to a young person, it can sound cute or dismissive depending on the situation.

examples.en: The contrabass is much bigger than the violin.
I play the contrabass in an orchestra.
My older brother is learning the contrabass at school.
The sound of the contrabass is low and heavy.
You need two people to move a contrabass.
The contrabass playing at the jazz concert was cool.

explain: '더블베이스'라고도 해요. 활로 켜는 악기라서 '콘트라베이스를 켜다'라고도 하고, 보통은 '연주하다'를 많이 써요. 클래식과 재즈에서 낮은 소리를 받쳐 주는 악기로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is also called '더블베이스' (double bass). Since it is played with a bow, you can say '콘트라베이스를 켜다', but '연주하다' is the more common verb. It often appears in classical music and jazz as the instrument that supports the low sounds.

examples.en: On cold days, you can see your breath from your nose as white mist.
The horse runs while snorting out breath.
The cat's breath touches my hand and it tickles.
He was angry and snorted heavily.
Breath from my nose fogged up the window.
The baby's breath is warm, so it feels nice.

explain: 입에서 나오는 숨은 '입김', 코에서 나오는 숨은 '콧김'이라고 해요. 화가 나거나 숨이 거친 모습을 말할 때 '콧김을 내뿜다/씩씩거리다'처럼 자주 써요. 소나 말처럼 큰 동물의 숨을 말할 때도 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Breath from the mouth is '입김' and breath from the nose is '콧김'. It is often used to describe someone angry or breathing hard, as in '콧김을 내뿜다'. It also fits well when talking about the breath of big animals like cows and horses.

examples.en: My younger sibling just snorted at what I said.

examples.ko: 그는 그 소문에 콧방귀를 뀌며 웃었어요.
examples.en: He laughed with a snort at that rumor.

examples.ko: 콧방귀 뀌지 말고 한번 들어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't scoff, just hear me out.

examples.ko: 아무리 설명해도 아버지는 콧방귀도 안 뀌세요.
examples.en: No matter how much I explain, my father doesn't even give it a snort of attention.
The boss scoffed at that proposal.
I heard him snort in contempt.

explain: 콧방귀는 거의 '콧방귀를 뀌다'라는 표현으로 나와요. 말을 믿지 않거나 우습게 볼 때 하는 태도라서, 윗사람이나 어른에게 하면 무례해 보여요. '콧방귀도 안 뀌다'는 아예 신경 쓰지 않는다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 내 충고에 콧방귀를 뀌었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 말을 우습게 여기거나 무시할 때 써요. 실제로 코로 소리를 내지 않아도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you dismiss or look down on what someone says. You can use it even if no actual sound is made.
phrases.en_equiv: scoff at; turn up one's nose at

explain_en: 콧방귀 appears almost only in the expression '콧방귀를 뀌다'. It is an attitude of not believing something or looking down on it, so doing it to elders looks rude. '콧방귀도 안 뀌다' feels like not paying any attention at all.

examples.en: Beads of sweat formed on the bridge of my nose.
My glasses left a mark on the bridge of my nose.
The child laughed, scrunching up the bridge of its nose.
The bridge of my nose turned red from the sun.
There is a small mole on the bridge of my nose.

examples.ko: 안경을 콧잔등까지 내려 쓰고 책을 읽어요.
examples.en: I read with my glasses sliding down to the tip of the bridge of my nose.

explain: '콧등'과 거의 같은 곳을 가리켜요. 땀이 맺히거나 안경이 걸쳐지는 곳을 말하는 장면에서 써요. 코 전체를 말하는 '코'와는 달리, 위쪽 볼록한 부분만 콕 집어 말해요.
explain_en: It points to almost the same spot as '콧등'. It is used in scenes where sweat forms or glasses rest on the nose. Unlike '코', which means the whole nose, it picks out just the raised upper part.

examples.en: I coated the injeolmi generously with soybean powder.
Soybean powder got on my clothes.
I roll the rice cake in soybean powder and eat it.

examples.ko: 콩고물 향이 고소해서 자꾸 손이 가요.
examples.en: The soybean powder smells nutty, so I keep reaching for it.
The soybean powder flew up and made me cough.

examples.ko: 떡 위에 콩고물을 솔솔 뿌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please sprinkle soybean powder lightly over the rice cake.

explain: 볶은 콩을 갈아 만든 고소한 가루로, 인절미나 떡에 묻혀 먹어요. 팥으로 만든 '팥고물'과 짝으로 같이 말하기도 해요. '콩가루'와 비슷한데 떡에 묻히는 고물은 '콩고물'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: If I join this construction project, I'll at least get some small share, right?
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰일에 가까이 있으면 부수적으로 작은 이익이 생긴다는 뜻이에요. 약간 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means that being close to a big deal brings a small side benefit. It has a slightly sarcastic feel.
phrases.en_equiv: get a small cut; pick up crumbs

explain_en: It is a nutty powder made by grinding roasted soybeans, used to coat injeolmi and other rice cakes. It is often mentioned together with '팥고물' (red bean filling or coating). It is close to '콩가루', but the coating for rice cakes is called '콩고물'.

examples.en: I took out the beans and threw away the pods.

examples.ko: 콩을 다 까고 나니 콩깍지만 남았어요.
examples.en: After shelling all the beans, only the pods were left.
The bean pods in the field are completely dried.

examples.ko: 할머니가 콩깍지를 벗겨 밥에 넣을 콩을 준비하세요.
examples.en: Grandma peels the pods to prepare beans for the rice.

examples.ko: 콩깍지가 바닥에 널려 있어서 쓸어 담았어요.
examples.en: Bean pods were scattered on the floor, so I swept them up.
The children played while shelling bean pods.

explain: 콩을 꺼내고 남은 껍질을 가리킬 때 써요. 일상에서는 사랑에 빠져 상대의 단점이 안 보일 때 하는 '눈에 콩깍지가 씌다'라는 표현으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 쟤는 눈에 콩깍지가 씌어서 남자친구 단점이 하나도 안 보여요.
phrases.en: She is so blinded by love that she can't see any of her boyfriend's flaws.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아하는 사람의 단점이 안 보이고 다 좋아 보일 때 써요. 놀리거나 걱정하는 투로 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone can't see the faults of a person they like and everything seems good. It is often said in a teasing or worried tone.
phrases.en_equiv: love is blind; be blinded by love

explain_en: It refers to the shell that is left after the beans are taken out. In daily life it also appears in the expression '눈에 콩깍지가 씌다', used when someone in love cannot see the other person's flaws.

examples.en: My heart pounds before the presentation.

examples.ko: 좋아하는 사람을 보면 심장이 콩닥콩닥하고 얼굴이 빨개져요.
examples.en: When I see the person I like, my heart flutters and my face turns red.
I watched a scary movie, and my heart is still racing.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 확인할 때 가슴이 콩닥콩닥했어요.
examples.en: My heart was thumping when I checked the exam results.
I ran here, and my heart is still pounding.

examples.ko: 첫 데이트 생각에 마음이 콩닥콩닥해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: Thinking about my first date makes my heart flutter, so I can't sleep.

explain: '두근두근'과 비슷한데 '콩닥콩닥'은 작고 빠르게 뛰는 느낌이라 설렘이나 긴장에 잘 어울려요. 보통 '가슴이/심장이 콩닥콩닥하다'처럼 써요. '콩닥콩닥 뛰다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '두근두근', but '콩닥콩닥' feels small and quick, so it suits excitement or nervousness. It is usually used as '가슴이/심장이 콩닥콩닥하다'. People also often say '콩닥콩닥 뛰다'.

examples.en: The child hops up the stairs with light thumps.
A rabbit is hopping around in the grass.

examples.ko: 가슴이 콩콩 뛰어서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: My heart was thumping so much that I couldn't speak.

examples.ko: 아랫집에서 천장을 콩콩 두드리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: I hear a light tapping on the ceiling from the downstairs neighbor.
I pounded the garlic in the mortar with light thumps.

examples.ko: 아이들이 한 발로 콩콩 뛰며 놀아요.
examples.en: The kids play, hopping on one foot.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 바닥이나 물건을 살짝 칠 때의 소리나 모양이에요. 더 크고 무거운 느낌은 '쿵쿵'이에요. '콩콩 뛰다', '콩콩 찧다', '콩콩 두드리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the sound or look of something small and light lightly hitting the floor or an object. The bigger, heavier version is '쿵쿵'. It is used as in '콩콩 뛰다', '콩콩 찧다' and '콩콩 두드리다'.

examples.en: I enjoyed reading the short story printed in the newspaper.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 짧은 콩트를 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: That writer wrote many short conte stories.
A conte is much shorter than a novel.
This short story has a twist at the end.

examples.ko: 동아리에서 콩트를 한 편씩 써 오기로 했어요.
examples.en: In our club we decided that each person will write one short story.

examples.ko: 방송에서 웃긴 콩트를 보고 크게 웃었어요.
examples.en: I watched a funny comedy sketch on TV and laughed out loud.

explain: '단편소설'보다 더 짧고 재치 있는 결말이 많은 글이에요. 요즘은 TV 코미디에서 짧은 연극처럼 보여 주는 것도 '콩트'라고 해요. 글인지 방송인지는 앞뒤 말로 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a piece of writing even shorter than a '단편소설' (short story), and it often has a witty ending. Nowadays a short skit performed on TV comedy is also called a '콩트'. You can tell whether it means writing or a show from the context.

examples.en: Someone is banging on the door.
I was startled by the crash of thunder.

examples.ko: 위층에서 쾅쾅 소리가 나서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: There were loud thumps from upstairs, so I couldn't sleep.
He got angry and pounded the desk.
They are hammering away with an iron hammer at the construction site.

examples.ko: 문을 쾅쾅 닫지 말고 살살 닫아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't slam the door; close it gently.

explain: 크고 단단한 것이 세게 부딪히거나 두드리는 소리예요. 작고 가벼운 소리는 '콩콩'이에요. 문을 '쾅쾅 두드리다'는 급하거나 화난 느낌이라, 보통 노크는 '똑똑'이 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the sound of something big and hard hitting or being struck hard. The small, light version is '콩콩'. Knocking '쾅쾅' on a door feels urgent or angry, so for a normal knock '똑똑' fits better.

examples.en: I wrote a card wishing our teacher a speedy recovery.

examples.ko: 며느리는 시어머니의 쾌유를 빌며 약을 정성껏 달였어요.
examples.en: The daughter-in-law carefully brewed the medicine, praying for her mother-in-law's recovery.

examples.ko: 친구가 입원해서 쾌유를 기원하는 꽃을 보냈어요.
examples.en: My friend was hospitalized, so I sent flowers wishing a quick recovery.

examples.ko: 다친 선수에게 팬들이 쾌유 메시지를 남겼어요.
examples.en: Fans left get-well messages for the injured player.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 쾌유를 위해 온 가족이 기도했어요.
examples.en: The whole family prayed for Grandpa's recovery.
I wish you a quick recovery.

explain: 주로 아픈 사람에게 카드나 메시지로 '빠른 쾌유를 빕니다'처럼 정중하게 인사할 때 써요. 가까운 친구에게는 '빨리 나아'라고 편하게 말해요. 보통 '쾌유를 빌다/바라다/기원하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used in cards and messages to a sick person, politely, as in '빠른 쾌유를 빕니다'. To a close friend, people say '빨리 나아' more casually. It usually appears as '쾌유를 빌다/바라다/기원하다'.

examples.ko: 표가 매진되기 전에 사서 쾌재를 불렀어요.
examples.en: I bought the ticket before they sold out and cheered inwardly.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 이기자 팬들이 쾌재를 불렀어요.
examples.en: When our team won, the fans cheered with delight.

examples.ko: 휴강 소식에 학생들은 속으로 쾌재를 불렀어요.
examples.en: The students cheered inwardly at the news that class was canceled.

examples.ko: 가격이 내렸다는 말에 쾌재를 부르며 가게로 달려갔어요.
examples.en: Hearing the price had dropped, I cheered and ran to the store.

examples.ko: 마지막 문제를 맞히고 나는 쾌재를 불렀어요.
examples.en: I got the last question right and shouted for joy.

examples.ko: 이런 기회라면 누구라도 쾌재를 부를 만해요.
examples.en: With a chance like this, anyone would have good reason to cheer.

explain: 거의 항상 '쾌재를 부르다'라는 꼴로 나와요. 일이 뜻대로 되어 속으로 통쾌할 때 써서, 겉으로 크게 소리치지 않아도 쓸 수 있어요. 대화보다는 글이나 이야기 속에서 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 이기자 팬들이 쾌재를 불렀어요.
phrases.en: When our team won, the fans cheered with delight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 뜻대로 되어 통쾌하고 기쁠 때 써요. 속으로만 기뻐할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things go as hoped and you feel thrilled. It can also mean being happy only inside.

explain_en: It almost always appears as '쾌재를 부르다'. You use it when things go your way and you feel thrilled, even if you don't actually shout out loud. It fits writing and storytelling better than casual talk.

examples.en: The sky is really clear today.

examples.ko: 날씨가 쾌청해서 소풍 가기 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: The weather is clear, so it's perfect for a picnic.
The rain has stopped, so the sky is clear.
They say it will be clear all over the country tomorrow.

examples.ko: 쾌청한 가을 하늘 아래에서 운동회를 했어요.
examples.en: We had a sports day under the clear autumn sky.
If the weather is clear this weekend, do you want to go to the Han River?

explain: '맑다'보다 구름이 거의 없이 상쾌하게 갠 날씨를 말해요. 날씨 예보나 글에서 자주 보이고, 보통 날씨나 하늘에만 써요. '맑다'는 물이나 눈, 목소리에도 쓰지만 '쾌청하다'는 그렇게 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It describes weather that is clear and refreshing with almost no clouds, which is stronger than '맑다'. It often appears in weather forecasts and writing, and it is used only for weather or the sky. '맑다' also works for water, eyes or voices, but '쾌청하다' does not.

examples.ko: 오래 닫아 둔 방에서 쾨쾨한 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: A musty smell comes from the room that has been closed for a long time.
The basement is damp, so it smells musty.

examples.ko: 젖은 수건을 두었더니 쾨쾨한 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: I left a wet towel out, and it began to smell musty.
The inside of the wardrobe smells musty, so I'm airing it out.
A musty smell rises from the old book.
When I opened the window, the stale air went away.

explain: 곰팡이, 먼지, 오래 묵은 것에서 나는 답답하고 안 좋은 냄새예요. '퀴퀴하다'와 비슷한 말이에요. 보통 '쾨쾨한 냄새'처럼 냄새를 꾸며 줄 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes a stuffy, unpleasant smell from mold, dust or things left a long time. It is similar to '퀴퀴하다'. It is mostly used to describe smells, as in '쾨쾨한 냄새'.

examples.en: The child fell down the stairs with a crash.

examples.ko: 위층에서 뭔가 쿠당탕 떨어지는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: I heard something crash down from upstairs.
The shelf collapsed with a clatter, and I was startled.
The loud crash startled me, and I ran to the room.
The cat ran off noisily and knocked over a flowerpot.
The parked bicycle fell over with a clatter.

explain: '쿵'은 한 번 묵직하게 울리는 소리이고, '쿠당탕'은 물건이 여러 번 부딪히며 요란하게 쓰러지거나 떨어지는 소리예요. '쿠당탕 넘어지다/떨어지다/쓰러지다'처럼 쓰고, 소리를 흉내 내는 말이라 대화에서 생생하게 들려요.
explain_en: '쿵' is a single heavy thud, while '쿠당탕' is a noisy sound of things bumping and falling over or dropping with several hits. It is used as in '쿠당탕 넘어지다/떨어지다/쓰러지다'. Because it imitates a sound, it makes stories vivid in conversation.

examples.ko: 아이가 손가락으로 반죽을 쿡쿡 눌러 봤어요.
examples.en: The child pressed the dough with a finger in deep pokes.
My younger sibling keeps poking my side.

examples.ko: 웃음을 참느라 쿡쿡 소리가 새어 나왔어요.
examples.en: I tried to hold back my laughter, but a snicker slipped out.

examples.ko: 감자가 익었는지 포크로 쿡쿡 찔러 보세요.
examples.en: Poke the potato with a fork to see if it's cooked.
My shoulder aches sharply, so I think I have to go to the hospital.
I'm digging the ground with a shovel in deep thrusts.

explain: 뾰족하거나 끝이 있는 것으로 깊이 찌르는 모습이에요. '콕콕'은 작고 가볍게 찍는 느낌이라 '쿡쿡'과 달라요. 웃음을 참으며 낮게 웃는 소리나, 몸이 욱신욱신 쑤시는 느낌에도 써요.
explain_en: It shows a pointed or tipped object being thrust in deeply. '콕콕' feels small and light, which is different from '쿡쿡'. It is also used for a stifled laugh and for the feeling of a throbbing ache.
